the settlement currency regardless of what is asked for here — see AgentBooking.currency_code.

traceId.description:
The agency's own correlation id for this attempt, carried into the platform's logs. Distinct from
`idempotency_key`: this one identifies the REQUEST for tracing, that one identifies the INTENT for
deduplication, and reusing a trace id is harmless where reusing a key is not.

wink.partner.v1.CreateBookingRequest.description:
Request for CreateBooking.

Shaped from the domain's CreateAgentBookingRequest rather than from what a single-room booking looks
like. `rooms` is REPEATED because the domain takes a list and because that is how a group booking is
made — the `group_id` that RefundBookings operates on exists precisely because one create can produce
several bookings. A one-room booking is a one-element list.

propertyId.description: The property to book at. From a Search or Inventory result.

checkIn.description: Local dates at the property, ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD).

roomRateId.description: The rate to book. From a pricing result's `RoomRate`.

bedroomConfigurationId.description: Which bedroom layout, when the rate offers more than one.

occupancy.description:
Who is in the room, and how many identical rooms of it. Child AGES are required rather than a count:
properties price children in age bands, and an unpriceable age produces a rate that cannot be booked.

promotionalCodes.description:
Promotional codes to apply. Silently ignored when they do not apply to this rate, which is the same
behaviour the booking engine has.

ancillaries.description:
Extras to add to this room — spa treatments, restaurant sittings, activities, add-ons, and the
in-room ancillaries sold with the rate itself.

guest.description: Who is staying in this room.

externalBookingCode.description:
The agency's own references, carried onto the booking and echoed back on reporting. These are the
reason an agent booking is its own request type: an agency reconciling Wink against its own system
needs its identifiers to survive the round trip.

externalFees.description: Fees the agency is adding on top of the rate. Amounts are in MINOR UNITS of `display_currency`.

wink.partner.v1.BookingRoomRequest.description:
One room to book.

Field-for-field from AgentBookingRequest, minus `nights` (derivable from the dates, and a second source
of truth for the same fact) and `vendor_specific` (a vendor-keyed metadata map, excluded for the same
reason its outbound twin is).

inventoryId.description: The thing being sold from — see the table above. Never a room type.

channelInventoryId.description:
Your channel's gate onto it. Empty when the item reached you through Wink Network rather than one of
your own sales channels, which is the common case and not an error.

offerId.description: The priced row you are buying.

type.description: Which kind of extra this is. INVENTORY_SCOPE_ANNOUNCEMENT is informational only and is rejected here.

quantity.description: How many. Bounded by the offer's `min_pax` and `max_pax` when it sets them; defaults to 1.

requestedStart.description:
OPTIONAL, and only meaningful for appointment-style extras — a spa slot, a restaurant sitting, an
activity departure — or where the offer's `pricing_type` is per hour or per day and the span is what
is being priced.

In-room extras and add-ons OMIT them: they are bundled with the stay, and sending times makes the
platform treat them as appointments and issue calendar invites nobody asked for.

These are REQUESTED, never confirmed. The property is not committing to them by accepting the booking.
ISO-8601 local date-time at the property.

wink.partner.v1.BookingAncillaryRequest.description:
One extra to add to a room.

Every field is quoted back from something the Inventory surface already handed you — there is nothing to
construct and nothing to look up. Where you read them from depends on which kind of extra it is:

  PROPERTY-LEVEL (restaurant, spa, meeting room, activity, attraction, place, add-on)
    inventory_id          AncillaryInventory.inventory_id          — the restaurant or spa itself
    channel_inventory_id  AncillaryInventory.channel_inventory_identifier
    offer_id              AncillaryOffer.id                        — the sitting, the 1-hour massage
    type                  AncillaryInventory.type

  IN-ROOM (INVENTORY_SCOPE_ROOM_TYPE_ANCILLARY)
    inventory_id          RoomRate.room_rate_id                    — the RATE, not a room type
    channel_inventory_id  RoomRate.channel_inventory_id
    offer_id              RoomRate.room_type_ancillaries[].id
    type                  INVENTORY_SCOPE_ROOM_TYPE_ANCILLARY

The in-room case is the one to read twice: its `inventory_id` is a RATE because the gate for these is
keyed by the master rate rather than by an entity. Sending a room type id there matches nothing, and it
does so SILENTLY rather than failing.

wink.partner.v1.BookingPerson.description:
A person on the booking. Deliberately not the platform's user model: an agency needs to contact somebody
about a stay, not to know their account.

amount.description: MINOR UNITS of the enclosing request's `display_currency`.

wink.partner.v1.BookingFee.description: A fee the agency is adding on top of the rate.

bookings.description:
One booking per room requested, in the order requested. A multi-room create produces several bookings
sharing a `group_id` — that is what makes them refundable together.

Repeated rather than singular because the domain returns BookingConfirmations, which is a LIST. A
single-booking response would have quietly dropped every room after the first.

idempotentReplay.description: True when this response replayed an earlier call rather than creating anything. Nothing was charged.

bookingCode.description: The human-facing reference shown to the traveller, e.g. on the confirmation email.

groupId.description: Present when this booking was made as part of a group; RefundBookings operates on this value.

status.description: Where the booking is in its lifecycle.

creation.description: How the booking came to exist.

createdAt.description: When the booking was created. ISO-8601 instant, UTC.

currencyCode.description:
ISO 4217 currency every monetary field on this message is denominated in. This is the SOURCE currency
— the one the property settles in — which is not necessarily the one the traveller was shown. See the
note on `net_total_sales_amount`.

booker.description:
Who booked it, and who is staying. Frequently the same person, and deliberately still two fields: an
agency books on behalf of a traveller far more often than not.

earnings.description: What the agency earns and what the sale was worth.

refund.description: Present once any refund exists, whether from a cancellation or an immediate refund.

comment.description: Free text captured at booking time.

earlyCheckInCharge.description:
Charges that apply outside the room rate — early check-in, late check-out and anything the property
adds. `has_additional_charges` is the cheap check; `additional_charges_summary` is the human-readable
detail when it is true.

customizationId.description:
The white-label configuration this booking was made through. The id only — the configuration itself is
the agency's own setup and is managed elsewhere, not published here.

statusHistory.description:
Status changes in order, oldest first. Enough to answer "when was this cancelled" without a support
ticket.

wink.partner.v1.AgentBooking.description:
One booking, as the agency that sold it needs to see it.

A deliberate projection, not a mirror of the internal model — see the note at the top of this file for
what is excluded and why.

phone.description: Direct contact for the property, for when the agency needs to call about a booking.

timeZone.description:
IANA zone, e.g. "Asia/Bangkok". Check-in and check-out below are LOCAL to the property, so without
this an agency cannot tell whether a same-day cancellation is still same-day.

wink.partner.v1.BookedProperty.description:
Who and where the property is. Flattened from a 670-line aggregate on purpose: an agency servicing a
booking needs to identify and contact the property, not to re-render it.

address2.description: Street line 2, when the property supplies one.

country.description: Country name in the requested language.

fullAddress.description: The full address pre-formatted for display, newline-free.

checkIn.description: Local dates at the property, ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD).

nights.description: Nights between them, precomputed so nobody has to reimplement the date arithmetic.

quantity.description: How many rooms of the above, and who is in each.

childAges.description:
One entry per child, carrying that child's age at check-in. Ages drive pricing, so an empty list means
no children rather than unknown ages.

netTotalSalesAmount.description:
Net sale value in `currency_code`, summed across SALE-type beneficiaries.

The SOURCE currency, meaning the one the property settles in. A booking sold in one currency and
settled in another carries an exchange spread, and that spread is intentional platform behaviour — do
not reconcile this against what the traveller was charged and expect equality.

netAmount.description: Net amount attributable to the booking after fees, in `currency_code`.

commissionPercent.description:
The agency's commission on this booking, as a percentage at booking time. Percentages rather than
amounts because that is how they are agreed and how they survive a partial refund.

agencyFeePercent.description: The agency's own agency-fee percentage at booking time.

commissionPercentAfterRefund.description:
Commission percentage restated after any refund. Equal to `commission_percent` until something is
refunded, and the value to reconcile against once something is.

wink.partner.v1.AgentEarnings.description:
What this booking is worth to the agency.

The agency's OWN economics only. The platform's fee, the supplier's agency fee and the payment
processor's cut are all deliberately absent — they are somebody else's commercial terms and publishing
them here would make them a contract we cannot change.

reason.description: Free text supplied by whoever cancelled.

source.description:
Who cancelled. An agency cancelling on the traveller's behalf and a property cancelling on the agency
are different conversations.

type.description:
The classification the cancellation was filed under, which is not the same thing as `reason`: this is
the closed list the platform reports on, that is what a human typed.

wink.partner.v1.BookingCancellation.description:
Why and when a booking was cancelled.

Field-for-field from the domain's BookingCancellation, minus `cancellerUserIdentifier` (an internal user
id an agency cannot resolve) and `groupRefundNotified` (a notification bookkeeping flag).

amount.description:
Amount returned, in `currency_code` minor units. This is the SOURCE amount — what the property
settles — matching every other monetary field on this message.

requestedAt.description:
When the refund was requested, and when it actually settled. `processed_at` is empty while the status
is PENDING or REQUIRES_ACTION, which is the honest answer: it has not been processed yet.

reason.description: Why it was issued, from the closed list, plus whatever free text accompanied it.

receiptUrl.description:
Processor-hosted receipt for the traveller, when one exists. Published because an agency fielding
"where is my money" needs something to forward; the processor's refund id and fee do not appear here
for the same reason no other payment plumbing does.

wink.partner.v1.BookingRefund.description:
Money returned, if any.

A cancellation does NOT imply a refund: a non-refundable rate cancels with nothing returned. Read this
message rather than inferring from `cancellation`.

checkIn.description: When the stay starts and ends. Both ranges are inclusive.

bookingCode.description: Exact match on the traveller-facing reference.

guestFirstName.description: Exact match, both optional and independent.

customizationId.description: Exact match on the white-label configuration the booking came through.

statuses.description: Restrict to these statuses. Empty means every status except the ones this service never returns.

pageNumber.description: Zero-based page index and size. Size defaults to 25 and may not exceed 100.

sortBy.description: Defaults to CREATED_AT descending, which is what the agent grid opens on.

wink.partner.v1.SearchBookingsRequest.description:
Request for SearchBookings.

Every filter is optional and combines with AND. Failed bookings are excluded server-side and there is
deliberately no field to include them.

There is also no affiliate filter, and that is a fix rather than an omission: the REST grid offers one
while the server independently pins the same field to the calling agency, so any value other than the
caller's own produces two contradictory equality filters and a permanently empty page. Scoping belongs
to the server.

wink.partner.v1.DateRange.description: An inclusive date range. Either bound may be omitted to leave that side open.

wink.partner.v1.SearchBookingsResponse.description:
Response for SearchBookings.

Wire mirror of the REST PageResponse envelope: `number` is zero-based and `total_elements` counts across
all pages, not this one.

reason.description:
Why the agency is cancelling, as free text. Carried onto the booking and, where the property supports
it, onto the reservation.

type.description: The classification to file it under. Defaults to CANCELLATION when unspecified.

booking.description:
The booking after cancellation. Read its `refund` to find out whether any money came back — a
non-refundable rate cancels with nothing returned.

sent.description: True when the email was handed to the mail pipeline. It does not promise delivery.

wink.partner.v1.ResendConfirmationRespon.description:
Response for ResendConfirmation.

Wrapped rather than returning a bare bool, so this rpc can gain a field later without a wire break.

idempotencyKey.description: Idempotency key. REQUIRED — a retried refund is a double refund.

reason.description: Why the refund is being issued. Recorded against the booking.

booking.description:
The booking after the refund has been applied. Read `refund.status`: a PENDING refund is settling
normally and must NOT be retried.

idempotentReplay.description: True when this response replayed an earlier call. Nothing was refunded again.

idempotencyKey.description: Idempotency key. REQUIRED, and it covers the WHOLE group so a retry cannot half-refund it.

outcomes.description: One entry per booking in the group, including the ones that could not be refunded.

idempotentReplay.description: True when this response replayed an earlier call. Nothing was refunded again.

error.description: Empty when the refund succeeded. Human-readable when it did not.

wink.partner.v1.RefundOutcome.description:
What happened to one booking in a group refund.

A booking that could not be refunded carries `error` and leaves `booking` populated with its unchanged
state, rather than failing the call — one booking outside its window must not deny the agency the
refunds it is owed on the rest.

propertyIds.description: Properties to fetch, 1 to 50. Identifiers come from a search result's `property_id`.

languageCode.description:
ISO 639-1 language for descriptions, e.g. "th". English is ALWAYS returned alongside it, so a missing
translation never leaves you with nothing to display. Defaults to English only.

include.description: What to include beyond the property's basic identity. Empty means basics only.

maxMediaPerEntity.description:
Cap on images and videos returned per entity. Zero means no cap, which is the default — you are
expected to cache the full bundle. Set this when you want a lighter response for a preview surface.

knownVersions.description:
Content you already hold: property identifier to the `cache_token` that property's last response carried.

A property whose token still matches comes back CONTENT_STATUS_NOT_MODIFIED carrying its
`content_version` and `cache_token` and nothing else — keep serving what you cached. Anything that has
changed, and anything you did not list here, comes back in full as usual. Omit the field entirely and
every property is returned in full, which is the default.

Send back the `cache_token`, NOT the `content_version`. The token is opaque: do not parse it, do not
build one, and do not assume anything about its length or alphabet. It covers the property's version AND
the shape of the request that produced it — your sales channel, `language_code`, `include` and
`max_media_per_entity` — which is precisely what makes it safe to widen a request. Ask for a scope you
did not have last time and the token stops matching, so you get the full response rather than a
NOT_MODIFIED that would have left you permanently missing the scope you just asked for.

BILLING DOES NOT CHANGE. You are charged one unit per call whatever comes back, so this saves response
size and processing on both ends, not money. Batching is what lowers a bill.

Entries for properties absent from `property_ids` are ignored, so you may keep one map and reuse it
across batches. At most 50 entries, the same bound as `property_ids`.

properties.description: One entry per requested property, in the order requested.

status.description: Whether content was returned, and if not, why.

contentVersion.description:
Version covering ALL static content for this property. The SAME value the pricing endpoints return on a
search result as `last_update`. Store it with your cached copy; re-fetch when a search shows a different
one. Present on CONTENT_STATUS_OK and CONTENT_STATUS_NOT_MODIFIED.

This is about the PROPERTY, so it is comparable across surfaces — but for that same reason it says
nothing about your channel, language or `include` set. To ask us whether your cached copy is current,
send `cache_token` rather than this.

includedScopes.description: The scopes actually populated below. Echoed back so you can tell "not requested" from "none exist".

property.description: Basic identity — always present when status is CONTENT_STATUS_OK.

details.description: Descriptions, address, policies, amenities and contacts. Present with CONTENT_SCOPE_PROPERTY_DETAILS.

restaurants.description: On- and off-premises restaurants. Present with CONTENT_SCOPE_RESTAURANT.

places.description: Places of interest. Present with CONTENT_SCOPE_PLACE.

cancellationPolicies.description:
Cancellation policies referenced by `RoomRate.cancellation_policy_id`. Present with
CONTENT_SCOPE_CANCELLATION_POLICY.

perks.description: Perks referenced by `RoomRate.perk_ids`. Present with CONTENT_SCOPE_PERK.

roomTypes.description:
Room types the property sells, ONCE each — not repeated per rate. Present when you request
CONTENT_SCOPE_ROOM_TYPE. `RoomTypeOffers.room_type_id` on the pricing surfaces points here.

ratePlans.description:
Rate plans, ONCE each — not repeated per rate. Present when you request CONTENT_SCOPE_RATE_PLAN.
`RoomRate.rate_plan_id` on the pricing surfaces points here.

counts.description:
How many of each ancillary entity this property has. ALWAYS present, whatever you included, and the
reason the default response is useful on its own: it tells you which scopes are worth requesting for
this property before paying for the round trip. A zero means the property has none, which is
information — an empty `restaurants` list would not distinguish that from "you did not ask".

cacheToken.description:
Opaque token identifying THIS response for THIS property. Store it and send it back in
`known_versions` to skip re-fetching content that has not changed. Present on CONTENT_STATUS_OK and
CONTENT_STATUS_NOT_MODIFIED.

Unlike `content_version`, this covers the request as well as the property: your sales channel,
`language_code`, `include` and `max_media_per_entity` all feed it. Two callers holding the same property
at the same version will hold different tokens if they asked different questions, which is why the token
is per-response and the version is per-property.

Treat it as bytes. It is not a timestamp, not a hash you should reproduce, and its format may change
without notice — a token we no longer recognise simply yields a full response, never an error.

wink.partner.v1.PropertyContent.description:
Everything requested about one property.

Populated fields depend on the `include` scopes you asked for. A scope you did not request is absent, not
empty — proto3 cannot distinguish "no restaurants" from "restaurants not requested" on a repeated field,
so check `included_scopes` rather than inferring from an empty list.

name.description: Property name in the requested language.

localName.description: Property name in its local language, when it differs.

starRating.description: Official star rating, 1-5. Zero when unrated.

images.description:
Published property images, lowest `sort` first. Capped by `max_media_per_entity` when you set one.
Unpublished assets are never returned — a property that took an image down did so deliberately.

videos.description: Published property videos, same ordering and cap as `images`.

currencyCode.description: ISO 4217 currency the property trades in.

wink.partner.v1.PropertyBasics.description: A property's basic identity — the same fields a search result carries.

descriptions.description: Localized descriptions, in English plus your requested language.

chain.description: Property chain, when the property belongs to one.

locationCategory.description: Setting, e.g. beachfront or city centre.

segmentCategory.description: Market segment, e.g. luxury or economy.

propertyCategory.description: Property type, e.g. property, hostel or resort.

whenBuilt.description: Year or period built, when recorded.

lifestyleTypes.description: Lifestyles this property is oriented toward.

policy.description: Check-in, check-out, children and pet rules.

totalReviews.description: Number of guest reviews behind the rating.

wink.partner.v1.PropertyDetails.description: Everything else about the property itself.

childrenMinimumAge.description: Minimum age accepted, when the property sets one.

petMaxWeightInKilos.description: Maximum pet weight in kilograms, when limited.

internetConnectionType.description: How internet is provided, e.g. wired or wireless.

internetConnectionLocation.description: Where internet is available, e.g. in-room or public areas.

internetAvailability.description: Whether internet is free or paid.

parkingAvailability.description: Whether parking is free, paid or unavailable.

parkingAccess.description: How parking is accessed, e.g. valet or self.

name.description: Item name in the requested language.

descriptions.description: Localized descriptions, in English plus your requested language.

sort.description: Display order within its collection, ascending.

onPremises.description: Whether the item is on the property's premises.

location.description: Where the item is, when it differs from the property.

address.description: Postal address, when the item has its own.

lifestyleType.description:
The lifestyle this item suits, when tagged. Singular, not a list: the platform records exactly one
per item.

amenities.description: Named features or amenities. Empty for attractions, places and add-ons, which do not record them.

wink.partner.v1.InventoryItemContent.description:
A non-room inventory item: restaurant, spa, meeting room, activity, attraction, place or add-on.

These share a shape deliberately. They differ in what they mean, not in what they carry, and one message
keeps the contract small and lets a client render any of them with the same code. Where a type needs
fields the others do not, those arrive as new field numbers on this message rather than a new message.

refundable.description: Whether the stay can be cancelled without charge before the deadline. The single field to branch on.

freeCancellationDaysBefore.description:
Days before arrival by which a free cancellation must be made. Zero means the deadline falls ON the
arrival day — read `advance_cancellation_free_of_charge` for the hour, which is the only place that
distinction survives. Absent on a non-refundable policy, which has no free window to count down.

advanceCancellationFreeOfCharge.description:
The free-cancellation window as the property set it, e.g. "SEVEN_DAYS_BEFORE_ARRIVAL" or
"UNTIL_EIGHTEEN_HUNDRED_HOURS_ON_DAY_OF_ARRIVAL". The two day-of-arrival values both report
`free_cancellation_days_before` = 0 and differ only here.

refundableCancellationCharge.description: What a refundable policy charges when the free window has closed, e.g. "FIFTY_PERCENT".

noShowCharge.description: What is charged when the guest does not arrive at all, e.g. "SAME_AS_CANCELLATION_FEE".

nonRefundableCancellationCharge.description: What a non-refundable policy charges on cancellation, e.g. "SEVENTY_PERCENT".

nonRefundableDeadline.description: The point after which a non-refundable policy charges more, e.g. "SEVEN_DAYS_BEFORE_ARRIVAL".

nonRefundableAfterDeadlineCancellationCh.description:
What a non-refundable policy charges once `non_refundable_deadline` has passed, e.g.
"ONE_HUNDRED_PERCENT".

wink.partner.v1.CancellationPolicyConten.description:
A cancellation policy: the deadline, and what is charged on each side of it.

Join to a pricing result through `RoomRate.cancellation_policy_id`. The pricing surface already tells you
whether a rate is refundable and until when; this tells you the terms behind that answer.

A policy has no name and no descriptions — it is a set of rules, not prose, and the platform stores no
localized text for one. Render it from the fields below; `policy_code` is the short label to show when
you have room for two characters and not a sentence.

The charge fields are enum NAMES, not free text, and the set of names is stable. Treat an unrecognised
value as "charge applies, terms unknown" rather than as an error: new members are added to these ladders
over time and an unknown one must not break your rendering.

id.description:
Stable room type identifier. Matches `RoomPrice.room_type_id` on the pricing endpoints, which you can
use to group several rates for the same room.

name.description: Room name in the requested language.

descriptions.description: Localized descriptions, in English plus your requested language.

sort.description: Display order within the property, ascending.

quantity.description: Rooms of this type at the property.

roomCategory.description: Room category, e.g. suite or standard.

amenities.description: Named amenities included with the room.

bedConfiguration.description: Bed configuration, e.g. one king or two twins.

wink.partner.v1.RoomTypeContent.description:
A bookable room type. Returned once per property in `PropertyContent.room_types`, never inline on a
rate; `RoomTypeOffers.room_type_id` points here. Only room types reachable from a master rate you can
see are ever returned by a property-scoped call.

id.description: Stable rate plan identifier. Matches `RoomRate.rate_plan_id` on the pricing endpoints.

name.description: Rate plan name as the property wrote it, e.g. "Best Available Rate". Untranslated.

prepaid.description: Whether the rate must be paid in full at booking rather than at the property.

breakfast.description: Breakfast is included in the rate.

brunch.description: Brunch is included in the rate.

lunch.description: Lunch is included in the rate.

dinner.description: Dinner is included in the rate.

allInclusivePlusAlcohol.description: Everything is included, alcohol as well.

cancellationPolicyId.description:
The cancellation policy governing this rate plan, when it sets one. Join to
`PropertyContent.cancellation_policies` or fetch it with GetCancellationPolicy.

wink.partner.v1.RatePlanContent.description:
A rate plan and what it includes. Returned once per property in `PropertyContent.rate_plans`, never
inline on a rate; `RoomRate.rate_plan_id` points here. Only rate plans reachable from a master rate you
can see are ever returned by a property-scoped call.

A rate plan has no localized descriptions — `name` is a single untranslated label the property chose,
and `language_code` on your request does not affect it. What a rate plan actually carries is what it
INCLUDES, which is the meal booleans below.

restaurants.description: Restaurants on and off the premises.

wink.partner.v1.PropertyCounts.description:
How many ancillary entities a property has, per kind.

Cheap to produce — these are stored counts on the property aggregate, not a count of loaded entities —
so they come back on every response regardless of `include`. Use them to decide which CONTENT_SCOPE
values are worth asking for: requesting CONTENT_SCOPE_SPA for a property with zero spas costs a round
trip and returns an empty list.

propertyId.description: Property to fetch. Identifier comes from a search result's `property_id`.

languageCode.description:
ISO 639-1 language for descriptions, e.g. "th". English is ALWAYS returned alongside it, so a missing
translation never leaves you with nothing to display. Defaults to English only.

include.description: What to include beyond the property's basic identity. Empty means basics only.

maxMediaPerEntity.description: Cap on images and videos returned per entity. Zero means no cap, which is the default.

knownVersion.description:
Content you already hold: the `cache_token` this property's last response carried.

Matches and the response comes back CONTENT_STATUS_NOT_MODIFIED carrying its `content_version` and
`cache_token` and nothing else — keep serving what you cached. Omit it and the property is returned in
full, which is the default.

Send back the `cache_token`, NOT the `content_version`. The same opacity rules as GetProperties apply:
do not parse it, do not build one. It covers the property's version AND the shape of the request that
produced it, so widening `include` correctly stops it matching rather than leaving you permanently
missing the scope you just asked for.

BILLING DOES NOT CHANGE. One unit per call whatever comes back.

wink.partner.v1.GetPropertyRequest.description:
Request for GetProperty.

The single-property mirror of GetPropertiesRequest. Field names match it exactly so moving between the
two is a shape change and never a semantic one — the only differences are that `property_ids` becomes a
single `property_id`, and the `known_versions` map becomes the one `known_version` it would have held.

property.description:
The property. Its `status` is CONTENT_STATUS_OK or CONTENT_STATUS_NOT_MODIFIED — an unknown id is a
NOT_FOUND error on the call itself, not a status here.

roomTypeId.description: Room type to fetch, from `RoomTypeOffers.room_type_id` on a pricing result.

languageCode.description: ISO 639-1 language for descriptions, e.g. "th". English is ALWAYS returned alongside it.

maxMedia.description: Cap on images and videos returned. Zero means no cap, which is the default.

ratePlanId.description: Rate plan to fetch, from `RoomRate.rate_plan_id` on a pricing result.

wink.partner.v1.GetRatePlanRequest.description:
Request for GetRatePlan.

No `language_code`: a rate plan carries a single untranslated `name` and no descriptions, so there would
be nothing for it to select. Accepting one anyway would imply a translation that never arrives.

cancellationPolicyId.description: Cancellation policy to fetch, from `RoomRate.cancellation_policy_id` on a pricing result.

wink.partner.v1.GetCancellationPolicyReq.description:
Request for GetCancellationPolicy.

No `language_code`: a policy is a set of rules with no stored prose to translate. See
CancellationPolicyContent.

term.description:
What the user has typed so far. Fewer than 3 characters (after trimming) returns an empty
list rather than an error.

wink.partner.v1.SearchRequest.description:
Your Wink account identifier. Every call is scoped to one account, and your token must hold
INVENTORY:READ on it.

destinations.description: Matching destinations, most relevant first. At most 50.

id.description: Wink's identifier for this destination entry.

type.description: What kind of place this is. Determines what `type_identifier` refers to.

typeIdentifier.description:
Identifier of the underlying resource — a property ID for DESTINATION_TYPE_PROPERTY, a geoname ID for DESTINATION_TYPE_CITY and
DESTINATION_TYPE_COUNTRY. This is the id you pass to the other Wink endpoints that take a property or place.

name.description: Display name, in the language given by `language_code`.

urlName.description: URL slug. Pass this back to the lookup-by-slug call to resolve this destination later.

ownerName.description: Display name of the supplier that created this entry, where one applies.

languageCode.description: ISO 639-1 code for the language `name` is written in.

longitude.description:
Longitude and latitude in decimal degrees. Both are omitted together when the location is
unknown — which is why they are optional rather than defaulting to 0/0, a real place in the
Gulf of Guinea.

wink.partner.v1.Destination.description: A place you can search for and sell through Wink.

urlName.description: URL slug of the destination, e.g. `bangkok-thailand`. Required.

type.description:
Type of the destination you are resolving. Required — a slug is only unique within a type,
so leaving this unset is rejected rather than guessed.

wink.partner.v1.GetRequest.description:
Your Wink account identifier. Every call is scoped to one account, and your token must hold
INVENTORY:READ on it.

userSession.description: Traveller context: dates, occupancy, language and currency. Required.

propertyId.description: Stable property identifier, as returned by Search and Lookup.

urlName.description: Url-safe slug, as returned by Search.

include.description:
Transactional inventory to price alongside the room offers. Leave it empty — the default — and you get
room offers only, which is the smallest response and what most booking flows need.

Each scope you add prices one more class of bookable item. Unrecognised values are ignored rather than
rejected, so a client built against a newer version of this file still works.

This does NOT change what you are billed: the meter counts hotel-days from the itinerary, not sections
of the response.

wink.partner.v1.GetPropertyInventoryRequ.description:
Request for GetPropertyInventory.

At most one of `propertyId, urlName` is set (protobuf `oneof property`).

currencyCode.description: ISO 4217 currency EVERY amount in this response is denominated in.

currencyExponent.description: How many decimal places `currency_code` has — amounts are `amount / 10^currency_exponent`.

languageCode.description: ISO 639-1 language the names in this response are in.

propertyId.description: Stable property identifier. Your key for everything, including Content lookups.

urlName.description: Url-safe slug, stable and safe to build links from.

uniqueId.description: The property's globally unique short code.

lastUpdate.description:
When this property's record last changed, ISO-8601 "YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss" in UTC. Use it as the cache key
for your Content responses — the same value Search returns.

available.description:
True if AT LEAST ONE offer is bookable for the requested stay. When false, `room_types` still carries
the unavailable offers rather than being empty, so you can show why.

commission.description:
Commission rate your account earns on this property, as a fraction — 0.15 for 15%. A property-channel
term, so it holds for every offer below.

roomTypes.description:
Offers grouped by room type. `room_types[0].rates[0]` is the best available price, the same figure
Search would have shown for this property.

perks.description:
Every perk referenced by any `RoomRate.perk_ids` below, deduplicated — one entry per distinct perk,
not one per rate. Resolve a perk id here rather than calling Content; a handful of distinct perks
typically cover every rate in this response.

addOns.description:
Every add-on referenced by any `RoomRate.add_on_ids` above, deduplicated the same way perks are.

Empty unless the request carried `INVENTORY_SCOPE_ADD_ON`. Unlike the collections below, add-ons are
NOT property-scoped: they are matched per room configuration, which is why the association lives on
each rate and only the priced rows are gathered here.

ancillaries.description:
Bookable non-room inventory at this property, one entry per item — a restaurant, a spa, a meeting
room. Each carries only its identifiers and its priced rows; everything describing the item comes
from Content, joined on `inventory_id`.

Contains only the types you asked for in `include`, and is empty when you asked for none.

announcements.description:
Announcements the property is running for the REQUESTED STAY — already filtered against your
itinerary, so everything here is meant to be shown. Empty unless the request carried
`INVENTORY_SCOPE_ANNOUNCEMENT`.

wink.partner.v1.PropertyInventory.description:
One property and every priced offer available for the requested stay.

For anything else about the property — name, descriptions, gallery, address, amenities, policies, and its
restaurants, spas, meeting rooms and activities — call the Content service with `property_id` and cache the
answer against `last_update`.

inventoryId.description:
Stable identifier of the item — the restaurant, spa, activity or add-on itself. Join to Content's
`InventoryItemContent.id` for everything descriptive.

type.description: Which kind of item this is, so a single flat list can be grouped without inspecting ids.

channelInventoryIdentifier.description:
Your channel's identifier for carrying this item. Present when the item reached you through a
distribution channel rather than directly.

commissionable.description: True if this item earns your account commission.

commission.description: Commission rate on this item, as a fraction — 0.15 for 15%. Zero when `commissionable` is false.

offers.description:
The bookable, priced rows for this item, CHEAPEST FIRST by `unit_price`. An item with no rows at all
is not returned, since it cannot be sold through this surface — Content is where you learn the
property merely HAS a spa.

Ordered for the same reason room rates are: a caller rendering "from ฿X" takes the first row, and an
arbitrary order would make that figure depend on the property's data-entry sequence.

wink.partner.v1.AncillaryInventory.description:
One non-room item the property sells, and its priced rows.

Deliberately thin. `inventory_id` is the SAME identifier Content returns as `InventoryItemContent.id`
for this item, so the name, descriptions, gallery, address, amenities and opening hours are one cached
Content call away and are never repeated here. What this message adds is the part Content cannot know:
what it costs, on your channel, right now.

descriptions.description:
Localized title and body together, in English plus your requested language. Whether the title should
be rendered is `show_title`.

showTitle.description: True when the property wants the title shown above the body; false to render the body alone.

wink.partner.v1.Announcement.description:
A message the property is running for the dates you asked to be priced.

Already resolved against your itinerary: a property's announcements each carry either a date window or
an "always show" flag, and both are evaluated server-side. Everything returned here is meant to be
displayed, so there is no window and no flag to re-check — publishing them would only invite each
integrator to re-implement the filter and get it subtly wrong.

entries.description:
The properties to price, each with its own dates and occupancy. At least one, at most 20.

Every entry must ask for the SAME `user_session.currency_code` and `user_session.language_code`, because the
response declares one display currency for all of them. A batch that mixes currencies is rejected with
INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than answered in a currency half the entries did not ask for.

properties.description:
One entry per request entry, in the order requested — match results back to your request by position.

The batch is ATOMIC. If any property cannot be resolved the whole call fails rather than returning a
short or reordered list, because a partial response that still looked well-formed would have you
attribute one property's prices to another. Nothing is billed for a failed batch.

currencyCode.description: ISO 4217 currency EVERY amount in this response is denominated in.

currencyExponent.description: How many decimal places `currency_code` has — amounts are `amount / 10^currency_exponent`.

languageCode.description: ISO 639-1 language the names in this response are in.

startDate.description: First check-in date to price, ISO-8601 "YYYY-MM-DD". Required.

periodInDays.description:
How many days forward to price from `start_date`. Between 2 and 30. Required.

This is also the billed unit count: a 30-day calendar costs 30 hotel-day units.

adults.description: Adults per room, between 1 and 10. Omit it to take the default of 2.

languageCode.description:
ISO 639-1 language for the room names, e.g. "en". Required: room names are translated against it,
and with no language supplied every name falls back to its untranslated form.

currencyCode.description: ISO 4217 currency for the returned prices. Exactly three characters.
ISO 4217 currency EVERY amount in this response is denominated in.

currencyExponent.description: How many decimal places `currency_code` has — amounts are `amount / 10^currency_exponent`.

languageCode.description: ISO 639-1 language the names in this response are in.

name.description: The property's name, in the requested language.

adults.description:
Adults every rate in this calendar is priced for — the occupancy you asked for, so it is the same for
every entry and is stated once here rather than repeated on each.

internetIncluded.description: True if internet is included across the priced rates.

parkingIncluded.description: True if parking is included across the priced rates.

entries.description: One entry per check-in/check-out combination in the range.

wink.partner.v1.RatePeriod.description: Best available rate for each check-in date across the requested range.

roomTypeId.description: Identifier of the room type this rate is for. Join to Content for its description, images and amenities.

name.description: The room type's name, in the requested language.

available.description: True if this combination is bookable.

refundable.description: True if it can be cancelled without charge before the policy's deadline.

refundableUntilDays.description:
Days from TODAY until free cancellation closes; -1 when not refundable, 0 when it closes today. Same
calculation as `RoomRate.refundable_until_days`.

total.description:
What the guest pays for this combination, in minor units of `currency_code`.

Only meaningful when `available` is true. An unavailable combination reports 0, which means "no price"
rather than "free" — do not render it as a price.

wink.partner.v1.RatePeriodEntry.description: The best available rate for one check-in/check-out combination.

wink.partner.v1.ListAccountsRequest.description:
Request for ListAccounts.

Deliberately empty: the response is scoped by your token alone. It exists so the call can gain
options later without a breaking change.

accounts.description: The accounts you can act for, up to 200. May be empty.

truncated.description:
True when you hold more than the 200 returned, so this list is incomplete. Switch to
SearchAccounts, which pages. It is false in every ordinary case; the list is never shortened
without setting it.

accountId.description:
Stable identifier for this account. Send it as the `managing-entity-id` metadata header on every
other call in this API.

ownerUserId.description: Identifier of the user who owns this account.

provisionedById.description: Identifier of the application that provisioned this account — normally Wink itself.

ownerType.description: Whether the account is held by a company or by an individual.

type.description: What kind of business this account is.

legalName.description: Registered legal name, when it differs from the display name.

urlName.description:
URL-friendly slug identifying the account in public profiles and links, e.g.
`the-siam-residences-bangkok`.

uniqueId.description: Short human-friendly identifier, used where a UUID would be unwieldy.

status.description: Where the account sits in its lifecycle. Only ACCOUNT_STATUS_ACTIVE accounts transact.

currencyCode.description: ISO 4217 currency the account accounts and settles in, e.g. "THB".

city.description: City the account is registered in.

logo.description: The account's logo, when it has published one.

wink.partner.v1.Account.description:
One Wink account — the business entity that owns properties, receives payouts and controls team
access.

This is an identity projection: enough to recognise an account, route a call to it and render it in
a picker. It deliberately carries no banking, payout or team-roster detail.

urlName.description: URL slug, e.g. `bangkok-thailand`. Accepted by Lookup's Get with DESTINATION_TYPE_CITY.

wink.partner.v1.AccountCity.description:
The city an account is registered in.

A projection of Wink's geographic record, not a free-text city name — `url_name` is the same slug
the destination Lookup service accepts, so you can resolve the full destination from it.

skip.description:
How many records to skip. Omit it to start at the beginning.

Paging is page-aligned, so this must be a whole multiple of `take` — 0, then `take`, then
`2 * take`, and so on. A partial offset is rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT rather than quietly
rounded down, so you can never be handed a page you did not ask for.

take.description: How many records to return. Between 1 and 180; omit it to take the default of 30.

status.description: Return only accounts with this lifecycle status. Omit it to return every status.

type.description: Return only accounts of this type. Omit it to return every type.

nameQuery.description:
Return only accounts whose name STARTS WITH this text, case-insensitively. Matched literally —
regular-expression characters carry no special meaning. At most 100 characters.

Prefix rather than substring on purpose: a substring match cannot use the name index and so reads
every account on the platform on a call that costs you nothing, which is not a load we are willing
to publish. Search for "Siam" to find "Siam Residences", not for "Residences".

sortBy.description:
Field to sort on. One of `name`, `urlName`, `status`, `type`, `createdDate` or `lastUpdate`;
anything else is rejected. Omit it to sort by `name`.

sortDirection.description:
Direction for `sort_by`. Omit it to sort ascending. Declared in partner_common.proto and shared
with the Booking surface, so ordering reads the same wherever you page.

accounts.description: The matching accounts for this page.

skip.description: Records skipped to produce this page — echoes the `skip` you sent.

take.description: Page size used — echoes the `take` you sent, or the default that was applied.

totalCount.description: Total accounts matching the filters, across all pages.

accountId.description: Identifier of the account to retrieve. Required. Your token must hold `ACCOUNT:READ` on it.

wink.partner.v1.LifestyleType.description:
The traveller lifestyle a property, room or media asset is oriented toward.

Values are additive: a property may carry several. Treat an unrecognized value as "some lifestyle this
client does not know about yet" rather than an error — proto3 enums are open, and new lifestyles are
added without a version bump.

- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_HEALTH_FITNESS`: Health and fitness focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_RELAX`: Relaxation focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_ADULT_ONLY`: Adults only.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_ADVENTURE`: Adventure travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_BUSINESS`: Business travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_LGBT`: LGBT focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_SINGLE_PARENT`: Single parent travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_SOLO_FEMALE`: Solo female travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_BEAUTY`: Beauty and wellness.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_FOODIE`: Food and dining focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_FAMILY`: Family travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_ROMANCE`: Romantic travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_COUPLE`: Couples travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_SOLO`: Solo travel.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_BACKPACKER`: Backpacking.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_SHOPPING`: Shopping focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_SPORTS`: Sports focused.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_MOUNTAIN`: Mountain destinations.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_BEACH`: Beach destinations.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_CITY`: City destinations.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_COUNTRY`: Countryside destinations.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_CULTURE`: Culture and heritage.
- `LIFESTYLE_TYPE_ECO`: Eco and sustainable travel.

wink.partner.v1.MultimediaKind.description:
Whether a Media entry is a still image or a video.

- `MULTIMEDIA_KIND_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set.
- `MULTIMEDIA_KIND_IMAGE`: A still image.
- `MULTIMEDIA_KIND_VIDEO`: A video.

wink.partner.v1.AdjustmentType.description:
The kinds of adjustment a rate can carry.

Mirrors the pricing engine's own buckets one for one. There is deliberately no "other": a new bucket
should appear here as its own member rather than being folded into a catch-all nobody can render.

- `ADJUSTMENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set; ignored.
- `ADJUSTMENT_TYPE_EXTRA_ADULT`: Surcharge for adults beyond the rate's included occupancy. Raises the price.
- `ADJUSTMENT_TYPE_EXTRA_CHILD`: Surcharge for children beyond the rate's included occupancy. Raises the price.
- `ADJUSTMENT_TYPE_SINGLE_OCCUPANCY`: Reduction for a room occupied by a single guest. Lowers the price.
- `ADJUSTMENT_TYPE_PREMIUM`: A rate premium the property attached to these dates or conditions. Raises the price.
- `ADJUSTMENT_TYPE_PROMOTION`: A promotion or promotional code. Lowers the price. This is the bucket a room-count deal lands in — a rate that only applies when you book three or more rooms is a promotion, not a separate kind.
- `ADJUSTMENT_TYPE_CHANNEL`: Your channel or membership terms. Lowers the price.

wink.partner.v1.PricingType.description:
How a non-room item is sold, and therefore how to multiply `AncillaryOffer.unit_price` up to a total.

Mirrors the platform's own pricing granularities one-for-one. Several combinations the names suggest
(per person per stay, per adult per use) do not exist because the platform does not offer them.

- `PRICING_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set; ignored. Treat a row carrying this as sold per stay.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_STAY`: Priced once for the entire stay.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_DAY`: Priced per day.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_NIGHT`: Priced per night.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_USE`: Priced per use or visit.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_HOUR`: Priced per hour.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_PERSON`: Priced per person.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_PERSON_PER_NIGHT`: Priced per person, per night.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_PERSON_PER_HOUR`: Priced per person, per hour.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_ADULT`: Priced per adult.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_ADULT_PER_NIGHT`: Priced per adult, per night.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_ADULT_PER_HOUR`: Priced per adult, per hour.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_CHILD`: Priced per child.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_CHILD_PER_NIGHT`: Priced per child, per night.
- `PRICING_TYPE_PER_CHILD_PER_HOUR`: Priced per child, per hour.

wink.partner.v1.ScoreSort.description:
How ranked results are ordered.

Four orderings, and they are the only four the platform actually has. Wink previously scored properties
on separate member, popularity, experience, perk, loyalty and add-on dimensions; those collapsed into a
single demand score in 2026-07 and their backing fields no longer exist. The REST enum keeps them as
deprecated aliases so persisted documents keep loading — every one silently resolves to RECOMMENDED —
but this contract is new, so it publishes only what it can honour. A sort you can select and that does
nothing is worse than one you cannot select.

- `SCORE_SORT_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set; the server picks RECOMMENDED.
- `SCORE_SORT_RECOMMENDED`: Wink's demand score — bookings and reviews blended, 0-100. The default.
- `SCORE_SORT_PRICE_LOW_TO_HIGH`: Cheapest first.
- `SCORE_SORT_PRICE_HIGH_TO_LOW`: Most expensive first.
- `SCORE_SORT_ECO`: Sustainability, highest first — backed by the green-index rating, which is maintained separately from the demand score.

wink.partner.v1.InventoryScope.description:
Optional transactional sections of a property-inventory response.

Every one of these prices something BOOKABLE. The names, descriptions, galleries, opening hours and
addresses behind these identifiers are static content and come from the Content service — call it once
per property and cache it. That split is the whole reason this surface stays small.

- `INVENTORY_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set; ignored.
- `INVENTORY_SCOPE_ADD_ON`: Add-ons purchasable alongside a room offer. Populates `RoomRate.add_on_ids` and the `PropertyInventory.add_ons` dictionary it resolves against.
- `INVENTORY_SCOPE_RESTAURANT`: Bookable restaurant inventory — tables, sittings, set menus.
- `INVENTORY_SCOPE_SPA`: Bookable spa inventory — treatments and sessions.
- `INVENTORY_SCOPE_MEETING_ROOM`: Bookable meeting and event room inventory.
- `INVENTORY_SCOPE_ACTIVITY`: Bookable activities.
- `INVENTORY_SCOPE_ATTRACTION`: Bookable attractions.
- `INVENTORY_SCOPE_PLACE`: Bookable places of interest.
- `INVENTORY_SCOPE_ANNOUNCEMENT`: Property announcements for the requested stay. Not priced, but itinerary-dependent, which is why it lives here rather than on Content: Content has no itinerary to resolve them against.
- `INVENTORY_SCOPE_ROOM_TYPE_ANCILLARY`: Extras sold with a ROOM RATE rather than by the property at large — the in-room ancillaries on RoomRate.room_type_ancillaries. Its `inventory_id` on a booking is the RATE's id, not a room type and not an entity. That is the one place this vocabulary is not entity-keyed, and getting it wrong produces an empty match rather than an error, so read BookingAncillaryRequest before using it.

wink.partner.v1.BookingStatus.description:
Where a booking is in its lifecycle.

Mirrors the domain enum exactly. `PAYMENT_SUCCEEDED` is the "booked and paid" state — there is no
separate CONFIRMED, and no COMPLETED: a stay that has happened is still PAYMENT_SUCCEEDED.

- `BOOKING_STATUS_INITIALIZED`: In flight. Never returned by this API — see GetBooking.
- `BOOKING_STATUS_TEST_PAYMENT_SUCCEEDED`: Paid against a test payment method. Returned so an agency can tell its own test bookings apart from real ones rather than discovering the difference in a reconciliation.
- `BOOKING_STATUS_PAYMENT_SUCCEEDED`: Booked and paid. The normal terminal state for a stay that goes ahead.
- `BOOKING_STATUS_FAILED`: Never returned: failed bookings are excluded from every response on this service.
- `BOOKING_STATUS_PARTIALLY_REFUNDED`: Refund states are STATUSES, not a flag on top of CANCELLED — a booking can be refunded without having been cancelled, so read the status rather than inferring from `cancellation`.

wink.partner.v1.BookingCreationType.description:
How a booking came to exist.

- `BOOKING_CREATION_TYPE_FAILED`: Never returned: failed bookings are excluded from every response on this service.

wink.partner.v1.CancellationSource.description:
Who cancelled.

Mirrors the domain's BookingCancellerType. Its `HOTEL` member is published as `PROPERTY` — the wire
vocabulary is deliberately generic and the naming guard enforces it, so the mapper is where the two
spellings meet.

wink.partner.v1.CancellationType.description: Why a booking was cancelled. Mirrors the domain's CancellationType.

wink.partner.v1.RefundStatus.description:
Where a refund has got to. Mirrors the domain's BookingRefundStatus.

- `REFUND_STATUS_PENDING`: Requested and settling. NOT a failure, and NOT to be retried — retrying a PENDING refund is how you refund twice.
- `REFUND_STATUS_CANCELED`: Spelled with one L, matching the payment processor and the domain enum.
- `REFUND_STATUS_REQUIRES_ACTION`: Needs intervention before it can settle; not terminal.

wink.partner.v1.RefundReason.description: Why a refund was issued. Mirrors the domain's BookingRefundReason.

wink.partner.v1.PaymentType.description:
How the booking was paid for.

Mirrors the domain enum. Two values, not a payment-method taxonomy: either the card was charged through
Stripe, or it came off the agency's own balance.

wink.partner.v1.BookingSortField.description:
What SearchBookings may sort by.

A closed list rather than a free-text field name, so the sortable surface is a contract instead of
whatever the storage layer happens to index today. These are exactly the columns the agent booking grid
offers.

wink.partner.v1.SortDirection.description:
Direction to sort a result set in.

Shared by every paged surface on this API, so one ordering vocabulary covers them all.

- `SORT_DIRECTION_UNSPECIFIED`: Never sent by the server; treated as ascending on a request.
- `SORT_DIRECTION_ASC`: Ascending.
- `SORT_DIRECTION_DESC`: Descending.

wink.partner.v1.ContentScope.description:
Which content to return.

- `CONTENT_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set; ignored.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_PROPERTY_DETAILS`: Descriptions, address, check-in/out policy, amenity and accessibility codes, contacts, categories.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_RESTAURANT`: Restaurants on and off the premises.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_SPA`: Spas.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_MEETING_ROOM`: Meeting and event rooms.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_ACTIVITY`: Activities.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_ATTRACTION`: Attractions.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_PLACE`: Places of interest.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_ADD_ON`: Purchasable add-ons.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_CANCELLATION_POLICY`: Cancellation policies and their deadlines.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_PERK`: Perks and their descriptions.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_ROOM_TYPE`: Room types the property sells, once each. Join from `RoomTypeOffers.room_type_id`.
- `CONTENT_SCOPE_RATE_PLAN`: Rate plans and their meal inclusions and terms, once each. Join from `RoomRate.rate_plan_id`.

wink.partner.v1.ContentStatus.description:
Whether a property's content could be returned.

There is no "not entitled" member, and its absence is deliberate. Content is not gated on your sales
channel — every property we hold is described to you. What your channel determines is which BOOKABLE
inventory comes back: `room_types`, `rate_plans`, `cancellation_policies` and `perks` are derived from
the master rates your channel carries, so a property you cannot sell returns CONTENT_STATUS_OK with its
descriptions, address and galleries, and empty bookable collections. That is a normal answer, not an
error — you are looking at a property you cannot currently sell, and `counts` still tells you what it
has.

- `CONTENT_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED`: Not set.
- `CONTENT_STATUS_OK`: Content returned.
- `CONTENT_STATUS_NOT_FOUND`: No property with that identifier.
- `CONTENT_STATUS_NOT_MODIFIED`: Your cached copy is still current — you sent a matching `cache_token` in `known_versions`. `content_version` and `cache_token` come back; every other field is absent, INCLUDING `counts` and `included_scopes`. Absent here means "unchanged, look at what you stored", not "empty" — do not overwrite your cache from this entry, and do not read `included_scopes` as the scopes narrowing to none. The token echoed back is the one to store for next time. You will only ever see this for a property whose token you supplied. It costs the same as any other entry: billing is per call.

wink.partner.v1.DestinationType.description:
What kind of place a destination is.

- `DESTINATION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`: Never sent by the server, and rejected on a request: pick a real type.

wink.partner.v1.AccountOwnerType.description:
Whether an account is held by a company or an individual.

- `ACCOUNT_OWNER_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`: Never sent by the server.
- `ACCOUNT_OWNER_TYPE_COMPANY`: A corporate entity.
- `ACCOUNT_OWNER_TYPE_INDIVIDUAL`: A sole proprietor.

wink.partner.v1.AccountType.description:
What kind of business an account is.

- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`: The account's type is not one this API publishes. Sent rather than omitting the account, so a new internal type can never make an account you manage disappear from your list.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_PROPERTY`: A hotel, resort, vacation rental or other bookable property.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_APPLICATION`: A software application integrating with Wink.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_TRAVEL_AGENT`: A travel agency.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_CORPORATE`: A corporate travel buyer.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_INFLUENCER`: A content creator monetising travel recommendations.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_BLOGGER`: A travel blogger.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_DESTINATION`: A destination marketing organisation.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_CHANNEL_MANAGER`: A channel manager distributing inventory on behalf of properties.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_PROPERTY_MANAGEMENT_SYSTEM`: A property management system.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_CENTRAL_RESERVATION_SYSTEM`: A central reservation system.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_GOOGLE_HOTEL_API`: A Google Hotel API integration.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_MANAGEMENT_COMPANY`: A company managing properties on their owners' behalf.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_CHAIN`: A hotel chain.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_BRAND`: A hotel brand.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_EVENT_ORGANIZER`: An event organiser.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_FACILITATOR`: A payment facilitator.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_DIRECT`: A direct-booking account.
- `ACCOUNT_TYPE_OTHER`: Anything that fits none of the above.

wink.partner.v1.AccountStatus.description:
Where an account sits in its lifecycle.

- `ACCOUNT_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED`: Never sent by the server, and ignored on a request: omit the field instead of setting this.
- `ACCOUNT_STATUS_PENDING_APPROVAL`: Created and awaiting compliance review; cannot transact yet.
- `ACCOUNT_STATUS_ACTIVE`: Fully onboarded and operating. The only status that transacts.
- `ACCOUNT_STATUS_INACTIVE`: Deactivated; no longer visible or transacting.
- `ACCOUNT_STATUS_UNDER_REVIEW`: Under compliance or quality review; some operations may be limited.
- `ACCOUNT_STATUS_SUSPENDED`: Temporarily suspended for policy violations or abuse.
- `ACCOUNT_STATUS_REJECTED`: Onboarding was rejected.
- `ACCOUNT_STATUS_REMOVED`: Permanently removed from the platform.

oauth2ClientCredentials.description:
Every endpoint is protected with OAuth2 **client credentials**. Create an
**Application** in your account to obtain a `clientId` and `clientSecret`, then
exchange them for a short-lived bearer token.

### 1. Request an access token
`POST` to the **Token URL** below with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
and a body of `grant_type=client_credentials` (optionally `scope=<space-separated scopes>`).
Send your credentials as HTTP Basic auth:
`Authorization: Basic base64(clientId + ":" + clientSecret)`.

### 2. Call the API
Pass the returned token on every request: `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

Tokens carry only the scopes granted to your Application — request the least privilege
you need. There is no interactive authorize step and no refresh token for this flow;
request a new token when the current one expires.
